name: sft-chained-on-iter4
hypothesis: Compound the iter4 ECHO +0.022 lift with SFT-ideal (r=8 α=16, all 188 gold-derived examples filtered to chars<2000, --max-examples 64) chained ON TOP of iter4. If lifts stack, expect +0.04 to +0.08; if invariant_coverage truly responds to gold-derived SFT, expect more.
verdict: REGRESSION — chained adapter performs WORSE than base (-0.055 at -1.35σ). Two of three seeds show large negative lifts (-0.084, -0.072). Format compliance and cross-file recall both dropped ~0.11; invariant_coverage dropped 0.107. Only grounding improved (+0.05).
lessons: SFT-on-iter4 with r=8 a=16 on gold-derived assistant outputs DESTABILIZES the iter4 base. The gold-format `<answer>{json}</answer>` strings are too narrow a target for stacked LoRA training — model overfits the gold's surface form and forgets iter4's invariant gains.

Adapter shape conversion (rank 16 → 8) plus --allow-adapter-shape-conversion may be silently re-initializing iter4 weights, washing out its prior gains. The chain is closer to fresh-SFT than true oscillation.

Oscillation (SFT→GRPO→SFT) is the listed methodology for this case, but kiln's current cuda_sft_file doesn't support adapter-stacking cleanly. A true SFT→GRPO ladder would need cuda_grpo_ablation with --base-adapter set to the SFT output.
implication: This rules out naive SFT-chain oscillation as a route to +0.10. Remaining methodologies on the goal's allowlist: agentic-GRPO with composite-shaped reward, or OPD with an external code-reasoning teacher. Both require substantially more pod time. With four orthogonal arms (iter4 ECHO, SFT-ideal, strict-prompt diag, SFT-chain) all sub-+0.04, the ceiling claim is well-supported.
